boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rowlett's Station (Woodsonville) record (December 17, 1861) in Operations in Eastern Kentucky [September-December 1861]. McCook's advance to Munfordville and the Green River bridge repairs are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the 32nd Indiana and gives the Confederates (Terry's Rangers, the 7th Texas Cavalry and the 1st Arkansas Battalion) about 1,350; the live field reads US 0 and CS 1,350. Hindman reports 1,100 infantry, 250 cavalry and four guns. Willich says 3 field, 1 staff and 16 line officers, 23 sergeants and 375 men took part against one Texas regiment, two infantry regiments and a six-gun battery at least seven times as strong. Hindman says the enemy crossed in force more than double his own, and that Terry charged about 300 with 75 Rangers.
claims.rationale: The CWSAC 1,350 equals Hindman's 1,100 and 250; its basis is not stated and the match is not corroboration. Hindman's report does not name a 7th Texas Cavalry. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live US zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General Thomas C. Hindman and Colonel August Willich. Willich was at division headquarters when the alarm came; Lieutenant Colonel Von Trebra ordered the companies forward, and Willich arrived later, took the right wing and ordered the fall-back signal. Hindman had gone to choose a camp, leaving Colonel Terry in command, and later withdrew his command.
claims.rationale: Both listed commanders were away when the fight began, by their own reports; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Indecisive. Willich says the Rangers disappeared in wild disorder and the enemy infantry and artillery withdrew in haste; Hindman says the enemy made no further attempt to advance and he withdrew knowing they had crossed in force; NPS says the Confederates withdrew knowing of McCook's approach.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 131 (US 40; CS 91). Willich reports 1 officer and 10 men dead, 22 wounded and 5 missing. Hindman reports Terry and 3 men killed and 4 dangerously and 6 slightly wounded, estimates the enemy's loss at 75 killed left on the ground and holds 7 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Buell's No. 1 dispatches and orders and McCook's No. 2 report (printed before Willich's; Buell's was glanced while delimiting, not selected), Johnson's indorsement, Hardee's orders printed with Hindman's report, returns and maps remain deferred. No nineteenth-century history covering the action was selected; this is a two-report or two-family first pass.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Willich's December 18, 1861 report is an interested Union account. Hindman's December 19, 1861 report is an interested Confederate account, the same author family as the registered Hindman McLemore's Cove reports. Both come from the Cornell OCR of Volume VII registered for the 1862 Eastern Kentucky pass. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
